summary: ORBITAL TRADE-OFF (Space Mission Architect) is an interactive educational video game designed to teach aerospace engineering through space mission planning and simulation. We developed a web application where players choose missions, select rockets and orbits, design satellites, manage resources, and solve engineering challenges. The game includes four missions: climate monitoring, global telecommunications, lunar exploration, and asteroid mapping. It addresses the challenge of making complex aerospace concepts easier to understand through interactive activities, realistic decisions, 3D graphics, animations, and cooperative gameplay for up to four players. It also includes different difficulty levels, random events, and educational questions. This project is important because it encourages scientific curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and teamwork while helping students understand the challenges involved in planning real space missions.
details: ORBITAL TRADE-OFF (Space Mission Architect) is an interactive educational video game that teaches aerospace engineering through the creation and simulation of space missions. The game allows players to design satellites, select rockets, choose orbits, and manage resources such as budget, mass, power, and communications. It includes four types of missions: climate monitoring, global telecommunications, lunar exploration, and asteroid mapping. It offers benefits such as developing logical thinking, encouraging creativity, improving decision-making, and promoting teamwork. The impact we hope to achieve is to spark students' interest in science, technology, and space exploration, making learning more fun and interactive. To develop this project, we used HTML, JavaScript, React 18, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and SVG graphics, as well as a computer to program and test the game. Its creativity is reflected in the 3D graphics, animations, challenges, unexpected events, and the possibility of playing individually or in teams of up to four people. Our team considered ease of use, visual design, functionality, learning, mission difficulty, and the balance of space resources. With this project, we aim to combine education and entertainment to teach how space missions are planned and developed.
